title: Add a local name in Pi-hole
summary: lab.home instead of 192.168.x.x — only after Pi-hole is already house DNS.

start.body: Pi-hole can answer a name you invent with the computer's house address. It only works for devices that already use Pi-hole as DNS. Not a public domain. Not a mesh kit.

choices.label: Phones already get ads blocked via Pi-hole

not-ready.body: Skip until a phone on house Wi-Fi already has ads gone. Point the router at Pi-hole first. A local name won't reach phones still using ISP DNS.

lock.body: Step 1: lock the number. hostname -I, then reserve that address on the router. A local name pointed at a moving number is how SSH and the share “break” after a reboot.

name.body: Step 2: pick a short name — lab.home, lab.lan, office.home. Prefer .home or .lan. Skip .local. Skip a real public site name.

add.body: Step 3: open http://pi.hole/admin → Local DNS. Domain: lab.home. IP: the reserved address. Add. Leave CNAME alone.

prove.body: Step 4: ping -c 3 lab.home or dig +short lab.home. Then ssh youruser@lab.home, smb://lab.home/photos, http://lab.home/admin. Wrong IP? Delete the row and add again.
